name: Axiom Systems Neural Interface Firewall NIF-3
product_name: Axiom Systems Neural Interface Firewall NIF-3
description: A hardware security module that installs between a user's neural interface and external data connections, providing real-time monitoring and filtering of all data entering or leaving the neural implant. The NIF-3 analyzes data packets for known attack signatures, anomalous patterns, and unauthorized access attempts, blocking threats before they reach the neural interface's processing core. The firewall includes anti-intrusion countermeasures that can trace and counterattack hostile connections, and a panic-disconnect that physically severs the neural interface from all external connections in an emergency.

specifications.monitoring: All data in/out of neural interface
specifications.installation: Inline with neural interface external port

story_hooks: A NIF-3's counterattack capability traced a hostile intrusion attempt back to its source — the attack originated from inside the user's own employer's network, revealing internal surveillance of augmented employees.

A firmware update to the NIF-3 introduced a vulnerability that it was supposed to protect against — the update came from Axiom's official channels, raising questions about whether the company is deliberately weakening its own security products.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, angular security module resembling a high-end network adapter with integrated heat dissipation fins. Sleek, defensive industrial design with prominent cable management ports. Feels like advanced medical hardware crossed with military-grade encryption tech.
physical_description.dimensions: 12cm length × 4cm width × 3cm height (roughly a thick smartphone)
physical_description.weight_description: Extremely lightweight (20g) — easily pocket-sized, worn on a belt clip or integrated into a neural rig harness
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade titanium alloy housing with embedded copper heat-sink fins; reinforced polymer connector shrouds
physical_description.finish: Brushed gunmetal with a matte non-reflective coating; thin anodized lines marking data flow direction; soft-touch rubberized grip edges
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with accent stripes in electric blue (active monitoring indicator) and red (threat/panic alert); subtle Axiom Systems branding in silver
physical_description.interface_elements: Dual redundant neural interface connectors (recessed, keyed); one status LED array (8-segment bar graph showing threat level); tactile panic button (recessed, requires deliberate press); micro USB for daily threat signature updates; secondary diagnostic port (maintenance-locked)
distinctive_features: Heat dissipation fins arranged in asymmetric pattern suggesting directional data flow
Dual-redundancy visual indicator: twin LED micro-arrays that pulse in opposition during active filtering
Recessed panic button with mechanical click-feedback and haptic confirmation
Transparent polymer window over internal circuit path showing layered PCB architecture
Military-spec connector locking mechanism with visible torque indicators
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Axiom Systems logo (embossed) on top; serial/batch number laser-etched on underside; regulatory stamps (GLMZ-certified, neural-interface-safe, warranty void if opened); threat-signature version number displayed on status strip
physical_description.condition_typical: In active use, mounted inline between a user's neural port and their primary data-link (usually worn on collar, wrist, or integrated into augmentation rig). Blue LEDs pulse steadily during normal operation; red LED flashes briefly when threats are detected and neutralized.
